entities.text: M/S. Firmenich Aromatics Production ... vs Vidya S B
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By the impugned Order the petitioner was prohibited from selling the articles, namely, (1) Cocoa powder, replacer flavour 1516SPM; and (2) Cocoa powder, replacer flavour 1728SPM under any name/Mode/Brand.

2. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the petitioner is carrying out business activities of "Relabeller Substances Added to Food" and "Manufacturer - Substances Added to Food", since last two years; and that the petitioner is doing the business, by obtaining appropriate licenses from the respondent No.1.

It is contended by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner that on the basis of a letter written to the Prime Minister's office regarding the products of the petitioner, the respondent No.2 conducted an inspection of the products of the petitioner in the factory on 8th October 2025.

It is further contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that on 9th October 2025,
903.WP-13588-2025 without even waiting for the Food Analyst report, the impugned order was passed by the respondent No.2.
It is the contention of the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner that the impugned order is passed in gross defiance of the principles of natural justice.
He submits that the petitioner has not contravened any process under the Food Safety Act or the Rules made therein.

Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner further contended that both the manufacturer, that is VKL and the relabeler i.e. the petitioner hold valid, subsisting FSSAI licenses and that the products in question are "Nature - Identical Flavouring Substances".
3.
Learned counsel for the respondent supported the impugned judgment and order.

She contended that upon scrutiny of the label specimen, brochure, copy, and the composition/ statement of ingredients and other documents, including license of the product, namely Cocoa powder, replacer flavour 1516SPM and Cocoa powder replace flavour 1728SPM, which are manufactured by M/s.
VKL Seasoning
Private
Limited
and 903.WP-13588-2025 marketed by the petitioner
, it was found that the petitioner had no valid license from the respondent.
She submits that thus there was violation of the conditions and labelling and display regulations.

Learned Counsel for the respondent further contended that there was no valid license for food, business activity of articles in question, nor was there compliance of the conditions of license, safety measures etc.

Learned Counsel appearing for the respondent,
however, stated that she requires some time to file an affidavit in reply of the respondents.
4. The learned Senior counsel appearing for the petitioner pressed for stay to the impugned order.
Both the parties argued at some length on the issue of grant of interim relief.

5. Heard the learned Counsels appearing for the parties.
6.

After hearing both the counsels for the parties, we are prima facie of the view, that the respondent No. 2 has failed to comply with provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Rules,

2 903.WP-13588-2025 2011.

entities.text: Firmenich Aromatics Production ... vs Vidya S B, Asst. Director, Desi. Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is true that the respondent No.2 is a designated officer appointed under Section 36 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and that he is bestowed with functions under Section 36 (3) (b) viz. to prohibit the sale of any article of food, which is in contravention of the provisions of this act and rules and regulations made there under, however, the Power under Section 36 (3) (b) of the FSSAI act 2006, has to be exercised in accordance with the rules made thereunder.
7.
In the present case, prima facie we are of the opinion that the rules, namely the Food Safety and Standard Rule 2011 are not followed by the respondents.
The applicant was not given a hearing.
It appears that the entire exercise was undertaken by the respondent, pursuant to a letter addressed to the PMO office by some person.
Prima facie, it appears that the entire exercise was carried out in a hurried manner.

8. We therefore, stay the effect, execution and implementation of the order dated 9th October 2025 (wrongly 903.WP-13588-2025 typed as 9th October 2024) issued by the respondent No.2, till the next date.

9. Let the affidavit in reply be filed by the respondents within a period of three weeks from today.
10. List the petition for admission on 27th November 2025.
All the concerned parties to act on the authenticated copy of this order.
(SANDESH D. PATIL, J.) (REVATI MOHITE DERE, J.) amraut M/S. Firmenich Aromatics Production ... vs Vidya S B, Asst. Director, Desi. Officer ... on 16 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123725018/
